items.title: Books on the History of Physics
items.body: I've just finished reading Quantum: Einstein, Bohr, and the Great Debate About the Nature of Reality by Manjit Kumar, which deals with the history of QM from Plank's quantisation for black body problem to Bell's inequality focusing especially on the debate between Bohr and Einstein as indicated in the title. Studying QM with mathematical background the book provides a perfect way to follow the advancements of QM step by step, though a layman could also understand the book since he explains very briefly the physical concepts aside. I'm looking for such books, with which I can study the history of physics and not the physics of some subject, which I already study in a more rigorous way.
